TCP Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-98432 / CVSS 9.8

TCP Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-98432 / CVSS 9.8

科技产品 作者 oger 热度 741 回复 332 2026/11/01 03:16
打开原帖 打开外部链接 JSON

摘要

  • Trevor Fannin@trevorfanninFounder, AtlasSecurity alerts and CVE breakdowns, plus infrastructure and general tech.Followon X (opens in a new tab) #Overview Linux's stable kernels shipped a fix on October 11 and 15, 2026 for CVE-2026-98432, a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP handshake that a remote, unauthenticated peer can reach. The kernel's own CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) scores it CVSS 3.1 9.8, Critical. The fixed releases are 5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10, and 7.3, and the bug goes back to Linux 4.4. The upstream fix is a four-line change, but most servers run a distribution's kernel. Red Hat, which now rates the bug Critical too, shipped fixed kernels for Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 8, 9, and 10 on November 1, and AlmaLinux followed on November 2. Ubuntu has shipped a fixed kernel only for 26.10: as of 3:15 PM CST on November 3, its fixes for 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04 are still in testing, and its tracker reads "Vulnerable" for every release, 26.10 included.
  • Why it's urgent: the bug sits in code every Linux server runs when it accepts an IPv4 TCP connection, before any application sees the connection. Anthropic, whose researcher reported it, says its Claude model wrote a working proof-of-concept exploit that runs commands as root on "Linux servers with a multipath TCP listener," with no credentials. Go programs open those listeners by default, per the Go Security Team. See the timeline. #Key facts FieldDetailCVECVE-2026-98432, "ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period," issued by the Linux kernel CNASeverityCritical, CVSS 3.1 9.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), the kernel CNA's score. Red Hat also rates it Critical, CVSS 3.1 9.8, raised from Important (8.1) on October 30. Ubuntu rates it Critical, raised from High on November 3. SUSE rates it important, and Oracle and Amazon rate it Important with CVSS 3.1 8.1.WeaknessUse-after-free of IPv4 option data during the TCP handshake (the record lists no CWE)ImpactPer the CNA's scoring notes: kernel heap contents disclosed to the remote peer, kernel memory corruption, or a crash. Red Hat's bulletin: a remote, unauthenticated attacker "could exploit a race condition during TCP connection request processing to trigger remote code execution."Fixed in7.2.10 and 6.18.56 (Oct 11) · 6.12.113, 6.6.159, 6.1.190, 5.15.223, and 5.10.272 (Oct 15) · 7.3 (Oct 18)No fix yetUbuntu 16.04 through 26.04, as of 3:15 PM CST, November 3; fixes for 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04 are in testing. Red Hat still lists OpenShift's RHEL CoreOS and a separate RHEL 9 real-time kernel package as affected. Upstream branches that reached end-of-life before 5.10 get no fix.Proof of conceptAnthropic says Claude built a remote root exploit for servers with a multipath TCP listener. It hasn't published the exploit.CVE recordsPublished on cve.org on October 15. NVD lists it as "Received," with no analysis of its own, as of 3:15 PM CST, November 3.CreditReported by Xinyang Ge of Anthropic. Fixed by Eric Dumazet and reviewed by Kuniyuki Iwashima, per the fix commit. #Who is affected Any Linux kernel from 4.4 on that lacks the fix, whether it serves the network directly or hosts containers: a container runs on the host's kernel, so a new image doesn't change anything. IPv6 connections aren't affected by the main issue; the commit says "IPv6 is not affected by the first issue." reissbaker 2026/11/01 08:54
This is not rare. Every TCP connection in Go by default enables MPTCP [1]. Simply running a Go program that uses TCP without explicitly disabling this behavior will cause the running kernel to be vulnerable.

1: https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/PCoQcdxoScw

hnlmorg 2026/11/01 18:11
> MPTCP port blocked

MPTCP doesn’t use any specific ports. It’s an OSI layer higher than that. It’s part of the TCP protocol itself. So if your firewall routes TCP traffic of a specific port (eg HTTP) already then it’ll route MPTCP along with it too.

ButlerianJihad 2026/11/01 18:14
MPTCP is a protocol extension that requires cooperation by both peers and all middleboxes. So, if there is a Layer 7 firewall, or DPI/SPI, or TLS termination on the path, and it's not inclined to preserve the MPTCP options, then MPTCP will be disabled.

hnlmorg 2026/11/01 20:43
Firewalls do not operate at layer 7 nor do TLS termination.

What you’re thinking of is load balancers. Most of them will do TLS termination. But there’s also plenty of load balancing solutions out there that will forward the raw TCP traffic (AWS NLB, DNS based solutions, and so forth).

But it’s also worth noting that this vulnerability doesn’t explicitly need MPTCP. Just the POC exploit uses that.
